split_definition.fold_algorithm: shuffle unique group labels with np.random.default_rng(seed), deal round-robin (gen5 seeded_group_kfold, via diversity_splits)
split_definition.test_set: the fold's held-out chemotypes; fixed, never acquired from
split_definition.start_cohort: the 10 most-measured training ligands of the largest training chemotype
split_definition.hard_chemistry_reference: the START cohort's extractants, frozen per fold

chemistry_cluster_definition.fingerprint: precomputed 2048-bit ECFP columns from the source table
chemistry_cluster_definition.ecfp_cluster: sha1 of the bit vector (bit-identical fingerprints)
chemistry_cluster_definition.source: rebuilt from the source table in this run

preprocessing.imputation: median + missing indicator, fitted on the revealed rows only
preprocessing.sample_weights: group_balanced_weights on the revealed rows' ecfp_cluster

preprocessing.reference: the START cohort of the fold
preprocessing.detail: computed once per fold before any acquisition and re-hashed at every checkpoint; see checks.hard_masks_fixed_per_fold

hypotheses.statement: Max-min diversity beats random acquisition on hard chemistry.
hypotheses.pass_condition: hard macro MAE(random) − hard macro MAE(maxmin) with CI95 low > 0 at ≥ half the checkpoints from 5 onwards.
hypotheses.falsifier: If maxmin is indistinguishable from random, the *choice* of ligand does not matter, only the breadth — Experiment B already showed breadth matters, so F1 dying reduces the deployable advice to 'buy any new chemotype'. An interval whose upper end is below zero would be stronger still: random would then be the better rule.

hypotheses.statement: Acquiring the most level-uncertain ligand beats random.
hypotheses.pass_condition: offset MAE(random) − offset MAE(offset_uncertainty) with CI95 low > 0 at ≥ half the checkpoints from 5 onwards.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the model's own level uncertainty is no better than chance — or no better than the chemistry-only maxmin rule — then the forest carries no acquisition information beyond chemical distance, and the cheap rule is the one to deploy.

hypotheses.statement: Buying more of the same chemistry is worse than random.
hypotheses.pass_condition: hard macro MAE(random) − hard macro MAE(same_chemotype_first) with CI95 **high < 0** (random is the better rule) at ≥ half the checkpoints. NOTE: the protocol table writes this as 'hard MAE(same_chemotype_first) − hard MAE(random), CI95 high < 0', which is the opposite of its own gloss 'i.e. random is better'; the gloss is scored here and the arithmetic is printed with every number so the reading cannot be hidden.
hypotheses.falsifier: If buying another analogue of what you already have matches random acquisition on hard chemistry, then the field's actual behaviour cost nothing measurable at this scale, and the generation's advice weakens to 'do not bother choosing'.

hypotheses.statement: Three measurements of a distant ligand beat three more of a known one.
hypotheses.pass_condition: the b = 3 maxmin curve lies below the curve that spends the same rows on the start cohort's own ligands, at ≥ half the checkpoints.
hypotheses.evidence: needs --f4-cap-start-rows; with the full start cohort there are no unrevealed start rows to buy, and Experiment B already measured depth vs breadth
hypotheses.falsifier: Not evaluated in this run. With --f4-cap-start-rows N it is evaluated against the depth_on_start arm; if depth matched breadth there, Experiment B's headline would be contradicted at the level of individual measurements.
